data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's conclusion that the log must require idempotency (not safety) depends on defining safety narrowly as 'no harmful side effects' (implementation safety). But SRC_001's own first countercondition concedes that if published literature defines safety to include 'no observable additional effect on retry,' then safety subsumes idempotency and the claim collapses. This is not a marginal edge case — retry-safety ('retriable without observable additional effect') is a well-established published concept. Since the problem explicitly asks to draw on published definitions, SRC_001 needed to either engage with this published definition of safety and show why it doesn't apply, or justify its narrow reading of safety over the retry-safety reading. Instead, the countercondition is raised but never resolved in the visible content, leaving the central conclusion unsupported under a valid published definition.
